summary: LLM inference costs scale directly with token consumption, and unoptimized production systems routinely overspend by 50-80% on redundant tokens, oversized models, and repeated context. Applying a layered strategy of prompt caching, semantic caching, model cascading, and prompt compression can realistically cut inference spend by 50-90% while often improving latency. The highest-leverage move for most teams is prompt caching, which cuts repeated input costs by up to 90% with minimal engineering effort.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (Provider-Native)
techniques.description: Reuse the processing of large static prompt prefixes (system prompts, instructions, documents) across requests so the provider charges a discounted rate for cached input tokens instead of reprocessing them each call.
techniques.example: Place your long system prompt and retrieved documents at the start of the message so OpenAI auto-caches the prefix, or add cache_control breakpoints in Anthropic's API to reduce input cost on repeated prefixes by up to 90%.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Cache full responses keyed by the semantic meaning (vector embedding) of a query rather than exact string match, serving cached answers for similar questions and skipping the LLM call entirely.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to embed incoming queries and return a stored response when cosine similarity exceeds 0.95, avoiding a full API call for paraphrased FAQs.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Route each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, escalating to larger models only when a small model's confidence or validation check fails.
techniques.savings: 40-80% reduction in average cost per request
techniques.example: Send simple classification queries to GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku first, and only fall back to GPT-4o or Claude Sonnet when the cheap model returns low confidence or fails a schema check.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Optimization
techniques.description: Shorten prompts by removing redundant instructions, trimming few-shot examples, and compressing context with tools like LLMLingua while preserving task-relevant information.
techniques.example: Apply Microsoft's LLMLingua to compress a 2,000-token RAG context down to ~800 tokens before sending it, cutting input cost by ~60% with negligible quality loss.

techniques.name: Max Output Token Limiting
techniques.description: Cap generated tokens with max_tokens and instruct the model to be concise, since output tokens are typically 2-4x more expensive than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and add 'Answer in one sentence' to the prompt for a summarization endpoint to prevent verbose, expensive completions.

techniques.name: Structured / Constrained Output
techniques.description: Force JSON or enum outputs via structured output modes so the model generates only necessary fields, reducing output verbosity and eliminating retries for malformed responses.
techniques.example: Use OpenAI's response_format with a JSON schema so the model returns only {"intent": "..."} instead of a paragraph explaining its reasoning.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Group multiple independent requests into a single batch job (or async batch API) to benefit from discounted batch pricing and amortized overhead.
techniques.savings: Up to 50% via batch API discounts
techniques.example: Submit 10,000 overnight classification tasks through OpenAI's Batch API to receive results within 24 hours at 50% off standard per-token pricing.

techniques.name: RAG Context Pruning / Reranking
techniques.description: Retrieve more candidate chunks but rerank and pass only the top few most relevant ones to the LLM, slashing the context tokens injected per query.
techniques.example: Retrieve 20 chunks from your vector DB, rerank with Cohere Rerank, and inject only the top 3 into the prompt instead of all 20.

techniques.name: Streaming + Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the required content or stop sequence is reached, avoiding paying for unneeded trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence of '}' when expecting a single JSON object so generation halts immediately after the object closes.

techniques.name: Fine-Tuned Small Models for Repetitive Tasks
techniques.description: For high-volume narrow tasks, use a small fine-tuned or distilled model that needs fewer in-context examples, dramatically shrinking prompt size and per-call cost.
techniques.example: Fine-tune GPT-4o-mini on 500 labeled examples so you drop the 1,500-token few-shot block from every classification prompt.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library that stores and retrieves LLM responses using embeddings and vector similarity to cut redundant API calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source (self-hosted; infra costs only)

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK that routes requests across 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, fallbacks, load balancing, cost tracking, and model routing.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source core free; Enterprise tier with SSO/support priced on request

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing caching, cost tracking, rate limiting, and request logging via a drop-in proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/mo and usage-based Enterprise

tools.name: Redis (Semantic Cache / LangCache)
tools.description: In-memory data store offering vector-based semantic caching for LLM responses to reduce latency and token spend at scale.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis OSS free; Redis Cloud free tier then usage-based, Enterprise priced on request

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in prompt caching (InMemory, SQLite, Redis, semantic) plus routing and retrieval components for cost control.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression tool that uses a small model to compress prompts up to 20x while preserving task performance.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway with semantic caching, routing, fallbacks, guardrails, and cost/observability analytics across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; paid plans from ~$49/mo and Enterprise pricing

tools.name: Cohere Rerank
tools.description: Reranking API that scores retrieved documents by relevance so only the most relevant chunks are passed to the LLM, reducing context tokens.
tools.pricing_paid: Trial free tier; production usage-based at ~$2 per 1k search units

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference engine with prefix caching and efficient batching for self-hosted open models to lower per-token serving cost.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source (self-hosted GPU infra costs only)

quick_wins: Enable provider-native prompt caching by placing static system prompts and documents at the start of every request to cut repeated input costs by up to 90%.
Add max_tokens limits and 'be concise' instructions to trim expensive output tokens immediately.
Switch default traffic to a cheaper model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku) and only escalate to a frontier model when needed.
Drop in a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) to serve repeated and paraphrased queries without any API call.
Route all traffic through a gateway like LiteLLM, Helicone, or Portkey to get caching, cost tracking, and fallbacks with minimal code changes.
